scope: ## 5. What the experiments showed that the spec text does not say

section_map.heading: ## 5. What the experiments showed that the spec text does not say

claim_checks.claim: Each is gated by a capability the server declares (tools, resources, prompts)
claim_checks.page_says: [14] "Servers that support tools MUST declare the tools capability"; [17] "Servers that support resources MUST declare the resources capability"
claim_checks.note: [18] says the same for prompts.

claim_checks.claim: In 2026-07-28 the declaration is returned by server/discover
claim_checks.page_says: "Servers that support prompts MUST declare the prompts capability in their DiscoverResult"
claim_checks.note: The cited page states this for prompts only; the sentence covers tools and resources too. True per [11] (DiscoverResult 'capabilities: Capabilities the server supports (tools, resources, prompts, etc.)'), which is not cited here. Fix: cite [11].

claim_checks.claim: Tools: functions the model can run | controlled by the model ("model-controlled")
claim_checks.page_says: "Tools in MCP are designed to be model-controlled, meaning that the language model can discover and invoke tools automatically"

claim_checks.claim: Tools methods: tools/list (paginated, cacheable), tools/call
claim_checks.page_says: "To discover available tools, clients send a tools/list request. This operation supports pagination and caching."
claim_checks.note: tools/call shown under 'Calling Tools'.

claim_checks.claim: Tools notification: notifications/tools/list_changed
claim_checks.page_says: "servers that declared the listChanged capability SHOULD send a notification to clients that have opened a subscriptions/listen stream with toolsListChanged: true"
claim_checks.note: The example notification's method is notifications/tools/list_changed.

claim_checks.claim: Resources: data identified by URI | controlled by the application ("application-driven")
claim_checks.page_says: "Each resource is uniquely identified by a URI." ... "Resources in MCP are designed to be application-driven"

claim_checks.claim: Resources methods: resources/list, resources/read, resources/templates/list
claim_checks.page_says: "To retrieve resource contents, clients send a resources/read request."
claim_checks.note: resources/list and resources/templates/list requests also shown on the page.

claim_checks.claim: Resources notifications: notifications/resources/list_changed, notifications/resources/updated
claim_checks.page_says: "The server delivers notifications/resources/updated on the resulting stream whenever a watched resource changes."
claim_checks.note: notifications/resources/list_changed shown in the List Changed example.

claim_checks.claim: Prompts: user-selected templates | controlled by the user ("user-controlled"), for example slash commands
claim_checks.page_says: "Prompts are designed to be user-controlled" ... "For example, as slash commands"

claim_checks.claim: Prompts methods: prompts/list, prompts/get
claim_checks.page_says: "clients send a prompts/list request" ... "clients send a prompts/get request"

claim_checks.claim: Prompts notification: notifications/prompts/list_changed
claim_checks.page_says: "SHOULD send a notification to clients that have opened a subscriptions/listen stream with promptsListChanged: true"
claim_checks.note: Example method is notifications/prompts/list_changed.

claim_checks.claim: Tool definition: name, optional title, description, inputSchema (JSON Schema object, never null), optional outputSchema, optional annotations, optional icons
claim_checks.page_says: "MUST be a valid JSON Schema object (not null)" ... "annotations: Optional properties describing tool behavior"

claim_checks.claim: Tool names should be 1 to 128 characters from A-Za-z0-9_-.
claim_checks.page_says: "Tool names SHOULD be between 1 and 128 characters in length (inclusive)."
claim_checks.note: Allowed characters list matches; modal SHOULD kept.

claim_checks.claim: Tool result: content blocks (text, image, audio, resource_link, embedded resource) and optional structuredContent (any JSON value in 2026-07-28; if outputSchema exists the server must conform)
claim_checks.page_says: "This can be any JSON value (object, array, string, number, boolean, or null) that conforms to the tool’s outputSchema if one is defined."
claim_checks.note: Also: 'Servers MUST provide structured results that conform to this schema.'

claim_checks.claim: Two error channels: protocol errors are JSON-RPC errors; tool execution errors come back as a result with isError: true so the model can self-correct
claim_checks.page_says: "Tool Execution Errors contain actionable feedback that language models can use to self-correct" ... "They are reported in tool results with isError: true"

claim_checks.claim: Resource contents are text or base64 blob. A missing resource is -32602 in 2026-07-28 (was -32002; clients should still accept -32002)
claim_checks.page_says: "servers MUST return a JSON-RPC error with code -32602 (Invalid Params)" ... "clients SHOULD also accept -32002 as a resource not found error"
claim_checks.note: [3]: 'Change resource not found error code from -32002 to -32602'.

claim_checks.claim: Prompt messages have role (user or assistant) and content (text, image, audio, resource link, embedded resource)
claim_checks.page_says: "role: Either “user” or “assistant” to indicate the speaker"
claim_checks.note: Content types listed on the page match.

claim_checks.claim: Pagination and cache hints (2026-07-28): list results carry nextCursor, ttlMs, cacheScope (public or private)
claim_checks.page_says: "cacheScope ("public" or "private") controls whether shared intermediaries may cache the response"
claim_checks.note: [14] example result carries nextCursor, ttlMs, cacheScope.

claim_checks.claim: Lists must not vary per connection. They may vary with the authorization presented on the request
claim_checks.page_says: "MUST NOT vary per-connection or as a side effect of other requests on the connection. The set MAY vary by the authorization presented on the request"
claim_checks.note: [14] states this for tools/list only; the claim covers all lists. The same rule is on [17] and [18] and in [3] ('List endpoints (tools/list, resources/list, prompts/list) no longer vary per-connection'), none cited here. Fix: add [17][18] or [3].

claim_checks.claim: Stateful tools use an explicit handle (basket_id from create_basket passed to add_item), because there is no session
claim_checks.page_says: "should do so by returning an explicit handle from a creation tool and accepting that handle as an argument on subsequent calls"
claim_checks.note: The page marks this section non-normative guidance; the claim is descriptive, not a requirement, so it passes.

claim_checks.claim: Standard utilities: completion (completion/complete for prompt and template arguments), pagination, progress, cancellation
claim_checks.page_says: not found: searched 'progress', 'cancel', 'cancellation' in [17], [18], [5]
claim_checks.note: [17]/[18] support the completion API and pagination only ('Arguments may be auto-completed through the completion API'). Progress and cancellation appear on [31] ('Progress tracking', 'Cancellation') and [7] (progressToken), which are not cited. Fix: cite [31] or [7] for progress and cancellation.

claim_checks.claim: Elicitation: server asks the user for input | elicitation/create, modes form and url; response action is accept, decline or cancel
claim_checks.page_says: "Elicitation supports two modes" ... "Elicitation responses use a three-action model to clearly distinguish between different user actions."
claim_checks.note: accept/decline/cancel listed.

claim_checks.claim: Elicitation 2025-11-25 status: active; also had notifications/elicitation/complete
claim_checks.page_says: "Remove the notifications/elicitation/complete notification and the elicitationId field of URL mode elicitation requests, both introduced in 2025-11-25."

claim_checks.claim: Elicitation 2026-07-28 status: active; that notification and elicitationId removed
claim_checks.page_says: "Remove the notifications/elicitation/complete notification and the elicitationId field of URL mode elicitation requests"

claim_checks.claim: Sampling: sampling/createMessage; optional tools/toolChoice when the client declares sampling.tools
claim_checks.page_says: "Clients MUST declare support for tool use via the sampling.tools capability to receive tool-enabled sampling requests."

claim_checks.claim: Sampling 2026-07-28 status: deprecated (SEP-2577)
claim_checks.page_says: "Deprecated: The Sampling feature is deprecated as of protocol version 2026-07-28 (SEP-2577)."
claim_checks.note: [21] registry row agrees.

claim_checks.claim: Roots: client tells server which file-URI directories matter | roots/list; notifications/roots/list_changed (legacy)
claim_checks.page_says: "Roots inform servers about the directories and files the client considers relevant"
claim_checks.note: [3]: 'Remove ping, logging/setLevel, and notifications/roots/list_changed.'

claim_checks.claim: Roots 2026-07-28 status: deprecated; notifications/roots/list_changed removed
claim_checks.page_says: "Deprecated: The Roots feature is deprecated as of protocol version 2026-07-28 (SEP-2577)."

claim_checks.claim: Roots are informational, not access control: "The protocol does not enforce that servers stay within roots"
claim_checks.page_says: "They are informational guidance rather than an access-control mechanism. The protocol does not enforce that servers stay within roots."

claim_checks.claim: MRTR: in 2026-07-28 a server must not send its own JSON-RPC request; it answers with resultType input_required, an inputRequests map (elicitation/create, sampling/createMessage or roots/list) and optionally an opaque requestState; the client retries with a new id, inputResponses and the echoed requestState
claim_checks.page_says: "inputRequests (optional): An InputRequests map of server-initiated requests that the client must fulfill."
claim_checks.note: The claim marks requestState optional but presents inputRequests as always present. The page makes both optional: 'Servers MUST include at least one of inputRequests or requestState'. Fix: say inputRequests is optional too, and at least one of the two is required.

claim_checks.claim: Only tools/call, resources/read and prompts/get may return input_required
claim_checks.page_says: "Servers MUST NOT send InputRequiredResult responses on any other client requests."
claim_checks.note: Table lists prompts/get, resources/read, tools/call.

claim_checks.claim: Worked example: tools/call id 2 returns input_required asking for a GitHub username via form elicitation; the client retries as id 3 with inputResponses github_login accept octocat and the same requestState
claim_checks.page_says: "Please provide your GitHub username" ... "Note that the JSON-RPC id MUST be different between the initial request and the retry."
claim_checks.note: [14] example uses ids 2 and 3 and the same requestState.

claim_checks.claim: Legacy equivalent: the server sent elicitation/create as its own request on the open connection or SSE stream, and the client replied with a JSON-RPC response
claim_checks.page_says: "This is a change from Streamable HTTP in protocol versions 2025-03-26 through 2025-11-25, where servers could send such requests on SSE streams."
claim_checks.note: [4] transports: 'The server MAY send JSON-RPC requests and notifications on the stream.'

claim_checks.claim: Subscriptions: subscriptions/listen is a long-lived request; filter has toolsListChanged, promptsListChanged, resourcesListChanged, resourceSubscriptions; first message must be notifications/subscriptions/acknowledged; later notifications carry io.modelcontextprotocol/subscriptionId (the request id); replaces resources/subscribe/unsubscribe and the HTTP GET stream
claim_checks.page_says: "The server MUST send notifications/subscriptions/acknowledged as the first message carrying the subscription’s ID in _meta under io.modelcontextprotocol/subscriptionId"
claim_checks.note: On stdio the ordering is per subscription, not per channel; the claim's summary still holds.

claim_checks.claim: Other methods removed in 2026-07-28: ping, logging/setLevel, notifications/roots/list_changed; log level is per-request _meta key io.modelcontextprotocol/logLevel. Logging is deprecated
claim_checks.page_says: "Remove ping, logging/setLevel, and notifications/roots/list_changed. Log level is now set per-request via io.modelcontextprotocol/logLevel in _meta"
claim_checks.note: [21] lists Logging as Deprecated (SEP-2577).

claim_checks.claim: Tasks moved out of core into the extension io.modelcontextprotocol/tasks
claim_checks.page_says: "Move experimental tasks out of the core protocol and into an official extension (io.modelcontextprotocol/tasks)."

claim_checks.claim: Quoted principles (same text in 2025-11-25 and 2026-07-28; 2025-11-25 adds a fourth on sampling): user consent and control; data privacy; tool safety (annotations untrusted unless from a trusted server; hosts must obtain explicit consent before invoking any tool)
claim_checks.page_says: "Hosts must obtain explicit user consent before invoking any tool"
claim_checks.note: Compared both overview pages: the three principles are word-for-word identical; [4a] alone adds 'LLM Sampling Controls'.

claim_checks.claim: Sampling controls (2025-11-25): users must approve sampling requests and control the prompt and what the server sees
claim_checks.page_says: "Users must explicitly approve any LLM sampling requests" ... "Users should control:"
claim_checks.note: The page uses 'must' for approval but 'should' for control of the prompt and results; the claim puts both under 'must'. Fix: 'users must approve sampling requests and should control the prompt and what the server sees'.

claim_checks.claim: The spec states MCP cannot enforce these at protocol level; implementors "SHOULD" build consent flows
claim_checks.page_says: "While MCP itself cannot enforce these security principles at the protocol level, implementors SHOULD:"
claim_checks.note: First item: 'Build robust consent and authorization flows into their applications'.

claim_checks.claim: The normative tools page uses SHOULD: "there SHOULD always be a human in the loop with the ability to deny tool invocations", with UI that shows exposed tools, visual indicators on invocation, and confirmation prompts
claim_checks.page_says: "there SHOULD always be a human in the loop with the ability to deny tool invocations.Applications SHOULD:"
claim_checks.note: The three UI items follow on the page.

claim_checks.claim: The one hard requirement on tool metadata: "clients MUST consider tool annotations to be untrusted unless they come from trusted servers"
claim_checks.page_says: "MUST be a valid JSON Schema object (not null)"
claim_checks.note: The quote is exact, but 'the one hard requirement' is not: the same page puts other MUSTs on tool definitions (inputSchema not null; x-mcp-header constraints, and clients 'MUST reject tool definitions where any x-mcp-header value violates these constraints'). Fix: 'the one MUST among the tools page's trust-and-safety statements'.

claim_checks.claim: Tools: servers must validate inputs, enforce access control, rate limit and sanitize outputs. Clients should confirm sensitive operations, show tool inputs before the call, validate results before passing to the LLM, apply timeouts, and log usage
claim_checks.page_says: "Show tool inputs to the user before calling the server, to avoid malicious or accidental data exfiltration"
claim_checks.note: Servers MUST and Clients SHOULD lists match the claim's modals.

claim_checks.claim: Resources: servers must validate URIs and sanitize file:// paths against traversal
claim_checks.page_says: "Servers MUST sanitize file paths to prevent directory traversal attacks when serving file:// resources"
claim_checks.note: 'Servers MUST validate all resource URIs' also present.

claim_checks.claim: Elicitation: servers must not request passwords, API keys, tokens or payment credentials in form mode; use URL mode instead
claim_checks.page_says: "Servers MUST NOT use form mode elicitation to request sensitive information such as passwords, API keys, access tokens, or payment credentials"
claim_checks.note: 'Servers MUST use URL mode for interactions involving such sensitive information'.

claim_checks.claim: Elicitation: clients must show which server is asking, offer decline/cancel, and for URL mode show the full URL and obtain consent before opening it; must not pre-fetch the URL; must open it in a way the client and LLM cannot inspect
claim_checks.page_says: "MUST NOT automatically pre-fetch the URL or any of its metadata." ... "MUST show the full URL to the user for examination before consent."
claim_checks.note: Decline/cancel and server identification are under 'MCP clients MUST:'.

claim_checks.claim: Elicitation: servers must not put sensitive data or pre-authenticated links in the URL, and must verify that the user who opens the URL is the user who started the request
claim_checks.page_says: "MUST NOT provide a URL which is pre-authenticated to access a protected resource" ... "the server MUST ensure that the user who started the elicitation request"

claim_checks.claim: Sampling (deprecated): human in the loop "SHOULD" be present; clients should let users review and edit prompts and responses
claim_checks.page_says: "Allow users to view and edit prompts before sending" ... "Present generated responses for review before delivery"
claim_checks.note: The page lets users edit prompts and review responses; it never says users edit responses. Fix: 'review and edit prompts, and review responses before delivery'.

claim_checks.claim: Multi round-trip state: requestState is attacker-controlled; if it affects authorization, resource access or business logic servers must protect its integrity (HMAC or AEAD) and reject failures; should bind it to principal, short expiry, originating request; once-only use must be enforced by the server
claim_checks.page_says: "servers MUST treat requestState as an attacker-controlled input. If requestState influences authorization, resource access, or business logic, servers MUST protect its integrity (e.g. HMAC or AEAD)"
claim_checks.note: SHOULD binding list and 'MUST enforce that invariant server-side' also match.

claim_checks.claim: Icons and schemas: icon URIs must be HTTPS or data:, fetched without credentials; clients must not auto-dereference $ref to a network URI
claim_checks.page_says: "Implementations MUST NOT automatically dereference $ref values that resolve to a network URI."
claim_checks.note: Icon items sit under 'Consumers of icon metadata MUST take appropriate security precautions'.

claim_checks.claim: Header trust: Mcp-* headers must match the body, otherwise 400 (prevents routing on a different truth than the one executed)
claim_checks.page_says: "Servers that process the request body MUST reject requests where the values specified in the headers do not match the corresponding values in the request body."
claim_checks.note: 400 Bad Request required on header validation failure.

claim_checks.claim: clientInfo/serverInfo are self-reported and must not be used for security decisions
claim_checks.page_says: "Implementations SHOULD NOT use them to change the behavior of the client or server, and SHOULD NOT rely on them for security decisions."
claim_checks.note: Both cited pages say SHOULD NOT ([11]: 'SHOULD NOT rely on it for security decisions'); the claim says 'must not'. Fix: 'should not be relied on for security decisions'.

claim_checks.claim: Definition: an MCP server accepts tokens it was not issued and passes them to a downstream API
claim_checks.page_says: "an MCP server accepts tokens from an MCP client without validating that the tokens were properly issued to the MCP server and passes them through to the downstream API"

claim_checks.claim: The spec forbids it: "MCP servers MUST NOT accept any tokens that were not explicitly issued for the MCP server"
claim_checks.page_says: "MCP servers MUST NOT accept any tokens that were not explicitly issued for the MCP server."
claim_checks.note: Exact quote.

claim_checks.claim: The authorization page adds that servers "MUST NOT accept or transit any other tokens" and that clients must not send tokens issued by a different authorization server
claim_checks.page_says: "MUST NOT send tokens to the MCP server other than ones issued by the MCP server’s authorization server." ... "MCP servers MUST NOT accept or transit any other tokens."

claim_checks.claim: If the server calls an upstream API it uses a separate token from the upstream authorization server
claim_checks.page_says: "The access token used at the upstream API is a separate token, issued by the upstream authorization server."

claim_checks.claim: Why: bypasses rate limits and audience controls, breaks audit trails, breaks trust boundaries, makes later security hardening harder
claim_checks.page_says: "Security Control Circumvention" ... "Accountability and Audit Trail Issues" ... "Trust Boundary Issues" ... "Future Compatibility Risk"
claim_checks.note: Rate limiting is named under Security Control Circumvention.

claim_checks.claim: Mechanism that enforces it: RFC 8707 resource at issuance plus audience validation at the server
claim_checks.page_says: "MCP clients MUST implement and use the resource parameter as defined in RFC 8707"
claim_checks.note: [26]: 'MCP servers MUST validate that access tokens were issued specifically for them as the intended audience'.

claim_checks.claim: Confused deputy applies to an MCP proxy server with one static client id that lets MCP clients register dynamically; with a third-party consent cookie, an attacker-registered client with an attacker redirect_uri plus a crafted link skips consent and the code goes to the attacker
claim_checks.page_says: "the third-party authorization server sets a cookie on the user agent indicating consent for the static client ID"
claim_checks.note: Attack steps on the page match.

claim_checks.claim: All four conditions must hold (static client id, dynamic registration, consent cookie, no per-client consent)
claim_checks.page_says: "This attack becomes possible when all of the following conditions are present:"
claim_checks.note: Four conditions listed.

claim_checks.claim: Mandatory mitigations ("MUST") for proxies: per-user client_id registry; MCP-owned consent page (client name, scopes, redirect_uri, CSRF, anti-framing); consent cookies with __Host-, Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, signed, bound to client_id; exact-string redirect_uri match; random single-use state stored only after consent
claim_checks.page_says: "Be cryptographically signed or use server-side sessions"
claim_checks.note: All items are MUSTs on the page, but the cookie item drops the alternative: the page allows signed cookies or server-side sessions; the claim makes signing mandatory. Fix: 'signed (or backed by server-side sessions)'.

claim_checks.claim: Mix-up: verify iss; PKCE alone does not stop it
claim_checks.page_says: "PKCE alone does not prevent this attack because the client transmits the code_verifier to the attacker’s token endpoint."
claim_checks.note: [26]: clients 'MUST apply the validation in RFC9207 Section 2.4'.

claim_checks.claim: SSRF through metadata URLs: clients should require HTTPS and block private ranges, and use an egress proxy on servers
claim_checks.page_says: "MCP clients SHOULD require HTTPS for all OAuth-related URLs in production environments" ... "operators SHOULD consider using an egress proxy"
claim_checks.note: Two qualifiers dropped: HTTPS is required 'in production environments', and the egress proxy is something to 'consider'. Fix: restore both qualifiers.

claim_checks.claim: Localhost redirect impersonation: authorization servers must display the redirect host
claim_checks.page_says: "MUST clearly display the redirect URI hostname during authorization"

claim_checks.claim: Dangerous authorization URLs (javascript:, shell-opening) must be rejected
claim_checks.page_says: "MUST reject javascript:, data:, file:, vbscript:, and other potentially dangerous schemes"
claim_checks.note: 'MUST NOT use shell commands (e.g., cmd.exe, sh, PowerShell) to open URLs'.

claim_checks.claim: Local-server one-click install: client must show the exact command and get approval
claim_checks.page_says: "Show the exact command that will be executed, without truncation"
claim_checks.note: 'Require explicit user approval before proceeding' under 'The MCP client MUST:'.

claim_checks.claim: 2026-07-28 has no protocol sessions; the security page names the risk 'state handle hijacking'; servers that authorize must verify every inbound request, must not treat a handle as authentication, should use cryptographically random handles, should bind handles to the verified user (<user_id>:<handle>)
claim_checks.page_says: "MCP servers MUST NOT treat possession of a state handle as authentication."
claim_checks.note: Verify-all MUST, random-handle SHOULD, and <user_id>:<handle> binding SHOULD all match.

claim_checks.claim: The tools page adds: a handle on an authenticated server "is a name, not a capability"; validate authorization on every call; state the retention policy in the creating tool's description
claim_checks.page_says: "For authenticated servers, a handle is a name, not a capability."
claim_checks.note: Retention-policy text: 'the server’s retention policy should be stated in the creation tool’s description'.

claim_checks.claim: 2025-11-25 sessions: id optional; should be globally unique and cryptographically secure, visible ASCII only, sent as MCP-Session-Id on every later request; server answers 400 without it, 404 after termination; client getting 404 must re-initialize; clients should DELETE when done
claim_checks.page_says: "Servers that require a session ID SHOULD respond to requests without an MCP-Session-Id header (other than initialization) with HTTP 400 Bad Request."
claim_checks.note: 400 is a SHOULD, and only for servers that require a session ID; the claim states it as fixed behaviour. The 404 (MUST), re-initialize (MUST) and other parts match. Fix: 'servers that require it should answer 400 without it'.

claim_checks.claim: 2025-11-25 security requirements: servers that authorize must verify all inbound requests and MUST NOT use sessions for authentication; session ids must be secure and non-deterministic; session ids should be bound to user data
claim_checks.page_says: "MCP Servers MUST NOT use sessions for authentication. MCP servers MUST use secure, non-deterministic session IDs."
claim_checks.note: 'MCP servers SHOULD bind session IDs to user-specific information.'

claim_checks.claim: Attack variants: session-hijack prompt injection across multiple servers sharing an event queue, and impersonation by a guessed id
claim_checks.page_says: "Server B enqueues the event (associated with session ID) into a shared queue."
claim_checks.note: Impersonation: the page says the attacker 'obtains' the id, and the mitigation text covers a guessed id.

claim_checks.claim: Experiment E6 shows the 400/404 behavior
claim_checks.note: Local experiment only.

claim_checks.section: ## 5. What the experiments showed that the spec text does not say
claim_checks.claim: The spec says a server must reject an unsupported version
claim_checks.page_says: "it MUST respond with an UnsupportedProtocolVersionError listing the versions it does support"
claim_checks.note: Role 6 claim citing Rank 1; taken because only 3 role-6 claims exist (k = 1).

claim_checks.section: ## 5. What the experiments showed that the spec text does not say
claim_checks.claim: McpServer + StdioServerTransport in SDK 2.4.0 is the legacy path: server/discover returned -32601 (E3); the modern path needs serveStdio (E4)
claim_checks.note: Local experiments only.

claim_checks.section: ## 5. What the experiments showed that the spec text does not say
claim_checks.claim: v1 SDK has no server/discover; its initialize negotiated an unknown version down to 2025-11-25 (E2)
claim_checks.note: The check mark carries no bracketed citation; only '(E2)' in the text points to a local experiment. Role 6, so this is not a citation failure, but a [E2] marker would be clearer.
